questions.question: What is the time complexity of Merge Sort in the worst case?

explanation.why: O(n) would mean a single pass suffices, but merge sort must divide and then merge across log n levels.
Each of the log n levels of recursion does O(n) work to merge, giving O(n log n) overall — and this holds in the worst case too, unlike quicksort.
O(n^2) describes simpler comparison sorts like bubble or insertion sort, not the divide-and-conquer structure of merge sort.
O(log n) alone would ignore the linear merge work done at each level of recursion.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about Merge Sort? (select all that apply)

explanation.why: The merge step can always take from the left sub-array first on ties, preserving the original relative order of equal elements.

options.text: It sorts in place with O(1) extra space

explanation.why: The standard merge step needs an auxiliary array to merge two sorted halves, so it uses O(n) extra space, not O(1).
Merge sort splits the array in half recursively (divide), sorts each half, then combines the results (conquer/merge).
